notice.title: Advance notice of fee increases
notice.aiSummary: Banks and credit unions must give consumers at least 60 days' written notice before increasing fees on deposit accounts. Firms must comply starting March 1, 2027.
notice.aiReason: The notice applies to banks that offer deposit accounts to consumers, and Brivanta Bank offers consumer checking and savings accounts.

text:
RETAIL CONDUCT AUTHORITY FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Final rule: Advance notice of fee increases
Notice number: RCN-2026-025
Issued by: Retail Conduct Authority
Published: 2026-11-16
Effective date: 2027-03-01
1. Who this applies to
Banks and credit unions that offer deposit accounts to consumers.
2. Background
Customers need time to compare products before a fee increase takes effect.
3. Requirements
3.1 A firm must give consumers at least 60 days' written notice before increasing a fee on a deposit account.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-03-01.

obligations.text: A firm must give consumers at least 60 days' written notice before increasing a fee on a deposit account.
obligations.controlDesc: Pricing change checklist confirms customer notices were sent at least 60 days before a fee increase
obligations.reason: Policy POL-FEE-02 states "Customers are given at least 60 days' written notice before any fee on a deposit account increases" which exactly matches the obligation's 60-day written notice requirement, and Control CTL-123 confirms this by verifying "customer notices were sent at least 60 days before a fee increase."
